newsitem.title: UK: English tops perk up in Bradford wool market.
newsitem.headline: English tops perk up in Bradford wool market.

text.p: Prices for finer tops reversed their recent gains, falling between ten and twelve pence per kg in a market which sources described as "confused" on Thursday.
Medium tops followed with losses of three to seven pence but quotations for English types were up an average of four pence.
The mixed picture reflected a choppy week for raw wool in the main markets, sources said.
British topmaking wools sold well at the UK auction this week, contributing to the price increases for English tops, they said.
But market nerves were rattled by the quarter-point increase in interest rates which helped the pound to a two-and-a-half year high on Wednesday.
"Export trade is very important to the UK tops industry and in this respect sterling strength is causing anxiety as prices become less competitive," one source said.
Currency factors were also said to be behind the increase in prices for fine and medium tops.
